finalText:
All 4 tests pass now.

## Root cause

`src/jobs/processOrder.js` called `pool.acquire()` directly and only released on the line after `run()`, with no `try`/`finally`. When an order failed validation and `run()` rejected, that release line never ran, so the connection leaked permanently — the pool has no timeout-based reclaim (`src/db/pool.js:3-5`).

The worker log shows the smoking gun: each `job order-XXXX failed: invalid order payload` line has no matching `connection released` line, unlike every successful job. Each failure permanently reduced the pool by one connection until it hit 0 available, triggering the cascading `pool exhausted` / `503` errors in both logs around 02:06–02:13, and the eventual supervisor restarts.

`src/handlers/api.js` was already safe — it uses the `withConnection` helper, which releases in a `finally` block.

## Fix

`processOrder.js` now routes through the same `withConnection` helper as the API handler, guaranteeing release on both success and failure. The stale comment about a removed retry loop (the original reason for the direct acquire) is gone too, since that reason no longer applies.
